coverage: The table lists differences among selected readings in prose verses.
The completed scan review covers stress helpers already present in MAM’s prose verses. It excludes a search for helpers absent from MAM and optional helpers in poetic verses.

The follow-up found differences from MAM at four additional verses. It completed all 10,223 pending scan checks, counting each occurrence in each edition separately. Both editions differ from MAM at 2Chr 20:27, which the earlier comparison had marked as an agreement in each edition. Koren differs from MAM at the other three verses.
The Decalogue comparison uses MAM’s manuscript-tradition תחתון for the Simanim Tanakh’s main Decalogues and its manuscript-tradition עליון for its appendix Decalogues.
The Simanim Tanakh has redundant pashta helpers on thirteen chanted words whose final syllable ends with two consonants bearing sheva. MAM has a single pashta, its usual notation for final stress.

source_notes.text: The comparison incorporates the Hebrew Wikisource correction at 2Sam 4:6. Koren, the Simanim Tanakh and corrected MAM have the telisha gedolah helper on the first he in וְ֠הֵ֠נָּה. The checked-in MAM-with-doc text still has the helper on nun.
source_notes.label: Wikisource correction

notes.text: The Simanim Tanakh has the telisha gedolah on qof and the gershayim on bet. MAM has both signs on both letters.
MAM’s notes describe the two cases where geresh or gershayim and telisha gedolah belong on different letters.
notes.label: MAM notes on telisha gedolah

notes.text: The MAM doc-note gives penultimate stress for MAM and Koren and final stress for the Simanim Tanakh, following Sephardic and Yemenite reading traditions.
The Simanim Tanakh adds a pashta helper within the final syllable. MAM indicates final stress with a single pashta.

MAM’s zarqa helper is on ḥet, at the start of the final syllable. The second occurrence of the same form in this verse has munaḥ on ḥet. Both printed editions have the postpositive zarqa alone on the first occurrence.
